steps.body: Radioactive decay runs on a **half-life** h: every h units of time, half the sample survives. The model: **N = N₀ · (1/2)^(t/h)**. Iodine-131's half-life is 8 days; 160 mg after 24 days is 3 half-lives: 160 → 80 → 40 → **20 mg**. The exponent t/h counts the halvings.

widget.prompt: 15 hours is three 5-hour half-lives. Slide the base to 0.5 and read base³.
widget.successFeedback: (1/2)³ = 0.125, and 240 × 0.125 = 30 mg. Counting half-lives is counting how many times the base multiplies in — three halvings, not a division by three.

steps.body: Fractional half-lives run through the formula's exponent. After 4 days with h = 8: N = 160·(1/2)^(4/8) = 160·(1/2)^(1/2) ≈ 160 · 0.707 ≈ 113 mg — about **71% survives** at the halfway mark, not 75%, because decay compounds. And 'how long?' questions fall to ln, exactly like every exponential equation.

explanationVariants: In N = 500·(1/2)^(t/12), the 12 divides t — it's the half-life; 500 is the start.
The denominator under t is always the half-life.

widget.prompt: For N = 500·(1/2)^(t/12), the starting amount and half-life are:

options.label: 500 and 12
options.feedback: Right — at t = 12 exactly one halving has occurred: N = 250.

options.label: 500 and 1/2
options.feedback: The 1/2 is the decay FACTOR per half-life — the half-life itself is the 12 under t.

options.label: 12 and 500
options.feedback: The coefficient out front (500) is the start; the t-divisor (12) is the half-life.

options.label: 250 and 12
options.feedback: 250 is the amount AFTER one half-life — the start (t = 0) is the full 500.

widget.prompt: N = 500·(1/2)^(t/12): how much remains at t = 36?

commonErrors.feedback: 36/12 = 3, so (1/2)³ = 1/8: 500/8 = 62.5 (dividing by 36 treats time as the divisor).

explanationVariants: (1/2)^(1/2) = 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 — about 71% survives at half a half-life, not 75%.
The halvings compound; the halfway survival is the square ROOT of 1/2.

widget.prompt: Half-life 8 days. What fraction survives after 4 days?

options.label: (1/2)^(1/2), about 71% after half of one half-life
options.feedback: Right — exponent 4/8 = 1/2, a square root of one half.

options.label: Exactly 75%, halfway between the starting and half amount
options.feedback: 75% averages the endpoints (100% and 50%) — decay compounds: (1/2)^(1/2) ≈ 70.7%.

options.label: Exactly 50%, because four days is enough for one halving
options.feedback: 50% takes the FULL 8 days — 4 days is only half a halving.

options.label: Exactly 25%, because the amount is halved twice
options.feedback: 25% is TWO half-lives (16 days) — 4 days leaves ≈ 71%.

explanationVariants: Match the halvings: four of them reach a sixteenth.

widget.prompt: Half-life 8 days. After how many days does 1/16 of the sample remain?

commonErrors.feedback: Multiply the half-life by the NUMBER of halvings (4), not by 16: 32 days.

explanationVariants: Take ln of both sides; two negatives divide to a positive count of halvings ≈ 1.74.

widget.prompt: Half-life 10 years. Using ln 0.3 ≈ −1.204 and ln 0.5 ≈ −0.693, after how many YEARS does 30% remain (one decimal)?

commonErrors.feedback: Multiply by the half-life 10: (1.204/0.693) ≈ 1.74 halvings × 10 = 17.4 years.
70% GONE isn't 7 years — solve (1/2)^(t/10) = 0.3 with logs: ≈ 17.4 years.

widget.fallbackFeedback: t = 10 · (−1.204)/(−0.693) ≈ 17.4 years; sanity: between 1 half-life (50% left) and 2 (25% left). ✓

hints: Set (1/2)^(t/10) = 0.3 and take ln of both sides.

steps.body: N = N₀(1/2)^(t/h): the exponent counts halvings.
takeaways: Whole half-lives: divide repeatedly; fractional ones: fractional exponents.
Half a half-life leaves ≈ 71%, not 75% — decay compounds.
Non-matching targets fall to ln, like every exponential equation.
steps.teaser: The finale: scales that measure earthquakes, acidity, and loudness — logs in the wild.

concept.body: Halvings one at a time: 80 mg with half-life 6 hours, after 12 hours. That's 12/6 = 2 halvings.

widget.prompt: 80 mg, half-life 6 hours: how many mg after 12 hours?

commonErrors.feedback: Divide by 2 twice (by 4 total), not by 12: 20 mg.
